definitions.explanation: A substance that produces a pleasant aroma when burned, used in religious ceremonies, meditation, and traditional Japanese culture.
A pleasant smell, especially from natural sources such as flowers, herbs, or wood.

examples.english: I burned incense in front of the Buddhist altar.

examples.japanese: ⟦{寺|てら}→寺：01676_tera⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{香|こう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{煙|けむり}→煙：02705_kemuri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ゆっくり→ゆっくり：00910_yukkuri⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{漂|ただよ}っていた→漂う：04356_tadayou⟧。
examples.english: When I entered the temple, incense smoke was slowly drifting through the air.

examples.japanese: {白檀|びゃくだん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{香|こう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{広|ひろ}がった→広がる：01980_hirogaru⟧。
examples.english: The fragrance of sandalwood spread through the room.
Drawn by the scent of plum blossoms, I went out into the garden.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 refers to the physical incense product and the act of burning it. Sense 2 is a literary or refined way to refer to pleasant scents, especially from nature. In everyday conversation, ⟦{匂|にお}い→匂い：00874_nioi⟧ or ⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧ is more common for general smells and fragrances.

CULTURAL NOTE:
⟦{香道|こうどう}→香道：29522_koudou⟧ (the way of incense) is one of the three classical Japanese arts of refinement, alongside ⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧ (tea ceremony) and ⟦{華道|かどう}→華道：04450_kadou⟧ (flower arrangement).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {香|こう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焚|た}く→焚く：02285_taku⟧ (to burn incense)
- {香|こう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{煙|けむり}→煙：02705_kemuri⟧ (incense smoke)
- ⟦{線香|せんこう}→線香：09995_senkou⟧ (incense stick)
- ⟦{香道|こうどう}→香道：29522_koudou⟧ (the art of incense appreciation)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧: fragrance, aroma — the more common everyday word for pleasant scents
- ⟦{匂|にお}い→匂い：00874_nioi⟧: smell, scent — neutral term for any smell, pleasant or not
